title: 3D characterisation of human skin tissue with various pathologies using innovative optical techniques to analyse tissue structures and cellular infiltrates in comparison with conventional histology
summary:
Chronic skin conditions such as Acne inversa often involve deep-seated inflammation beneath the skin. This inflammation forms painful lumps, abscesses and sometimes tunnels in the tissue, which can recur repeatedly and leave scars. Because the condition is so deep within the tissue, it often heals poorly and is initially easily mistaken for ordinary abscesses. An early diagnosis helps to alleviate symptoms and prevent further damage. 
Two state-of-the-art imaging techniques are to be tested, which could help doctors detect Acne inversa and other skin diseases at an early stage in small tissue samples (biopsies) or even directly on the skin:
(1) Multiphoton microscopy uses laser light that can penetrate deep into the skin. This makes it possible to visualise, for example, early-stage inflammation, damaged hair follicles or changes in connective tissue – which are often not detectable with the naked eye or conventional methods. This type of microscopy could provide additional information about the nature of the tissue in biopsies or surgical specimens, helping to treat Acne inversa more effectively and distinguish it from other skin conditions.
(2) Fluorescence lifetime imaging measures how long certain molecules in the skin continue to emit light, which provides insights into metabolic processes and inflammatory reactions. This procedure is completely painless and could, in future, aid in the early diagnosis of Acne inversa and help distinguish the condition from other skin diseases.  The suitability of this method is to be tested on Acne inversa tissue samples before it is further developed for use directly on the skin. 
Together, both methods provide a very accurate picture of what is happening in the deep layers of the skin, long before abscesses, fistulas or scars develop. As a result, they could help to diagnose Acne inversa earlier in the future, better assess the severity of the condition and plan appropriate treatments more quickly.
conditions: Diseases of the skin and subcutaneous tissue

interventions.name: Surplus material (from skin biopsies and skin tissue removed during surgery), the use of which patients have consented to as part of a consent form for the research project, is scanned using two innovative imaging devices.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
All patients who have signed a consent form for the research project and have therefore consented to the further use of their own tissue or that of their child for research purposes.
Exclusion criteria:
All patients who have not signed a consent form for the research project and who have therefore not consented to the further use of their own or their child’s tissue for research purposes within the study.
